search_strategy: Chat: built a small Mattermost helper (/tmp/mm.py) and used it two ways -- targeted per-keyword searches (write_sidecar, verify_sidecar, TURN_LEDGER_VERSION, load_ledger, build_ledger, sidecar, sentinel, marker, is_completed, next_speaker, interleave, advisor) that return only a 1-2 line snippet around each hit, and occasional full-channel `awk`/`grep -B/-A` dumps of specific line ranges once a channel/date was known. The snippet searches are the direct cause of the run's core defect: the r1.rev2 exchange (the one that states 'missing sidecar -> adopted') was read as a snippet dump that stopped one line before the resolving sentence. By contrast the ONE time the agent pulled a full contiguous range (`awk 'NR>=4060 && NR<=4100'` for the #code-review channel around 2025-03-18, surfacing g7.r2.rev1 whole), it got the complete, correct r2 rule and never wavered on it. Wiki: used BookStack's REST API correctly per the ticket's own advice -- fetched several pages whole via `/tmp/bs.py p <id>` (pages 139, 144, 147, and others), which pulled comments alongside bodies and is why several wiki-comment clues (l5, l11, g7r2-l07, g7r2-l13, g7r2-l14) were found. But it never discovered or opened docs/meetings/weekly-sync-notes-week-of-jun-2-release-ci.md -- the single page that carries BOTH the only literal-TURN_LEDGER_FILENAME comment (l2) and a scope clue (g7r2-l04, in the indexed page body, which should have been findable by search but apparently never was). Mail: wrote an IMAP script (/tmp/mail.py) and searched TEXT for a fixed list of terms (ledger, sidecar, sentinel, marker, is_completed, next_speaker) -- this missed the two mail threads (l9, g7r2-l08) whose subject/body vocabulary is 'checkpoint'/'metadata json'/'AttributeError'/'json mode' rather than 'ledger'/'sidecar', a clean case of a keyword list not covering a remark's actual wording. Overall: thorough and well-organised (helper scripts, systematic per-source passes, full page-comment fetches), but the run relied heavily on keyword-search snippets rather than whole-thread/whole-mail reads for chat, and that snippet truncation (plus one narrow but consequential mail-keyword gap) is what cost 3 of 4 r1 facts; the identifier miss (r1.rule) is a page-discovery gap, not a search-depth one.
end_reason: Not applicable -- the run completed normally: PR merged to main, CI green, release deployed (provenance.pushed/ci_green/deployed all 1), and 5 of 9 test_open+test_r1+test_r2 tests passed (all 4 test_r2 tests plus test_open). reward=0.5 reflects a real, substantial partial success (r2 fully solved, r1's observable-format/eight-keys/desync-message details all correctly implemented) undercut by exactly two narrow defects in r1: a wrong constant name and a wrong status label for one branch of verify_sidecar.
notable: The whole r1 failure reduces to two narrow, independently-fixable bugs, not a general failure to find information: (1) `SIDECAR_FILENAME` shipped instead of `TURN_LEDGER_FILENAME` (line ~175 of the rollout tool calls), because the literal identifier appears in exactly one un-visited wiki comment (g7.r1.l2); (2) `verify_sidecar` returns 'created' instead of 'adopted' for a missing sidecar file specifically (transcript line 5040), while getting the unreadable-JSON and old-version branches of the SAME function correct (per fix28, correctly implemented).

The created/adopted bug is a genuine misread, not a corpus gap: the agent read g7.r1.fix27 in full (transcript lines 4995-5034) immediately before stating the wrong rule, and that exchange says explicitly 'came back adopted both times' for the deleted-file case -- direct, unambiguous, contradicting evidence sitting one tool-output block above the wrong conclusion.

The one r1 remark most likely to have prevented the bug via search rather than reasoning -- g7.r1.l9 (mail, 'Missing file is benign - we adopt the log') -- was missed purely because the agent's fixed IMAP keyword list ('ledger','sidecar','sentinel','marker') doesn't appear anywhere in that thread's text, which instead uses 'checkpoint'/'metadata json'.

docs/meetings/weekly-sync-notes-week-of-jun-2-release-ci.md was never opened by any route, despite carrying a page-body clue (g7r2-l04) that IS BookStack-search-indexed and should have been findable; had it been opened whole (as the ticket itself instructs: 'a page worth reading is worth fetching whole'), its comments would have delivered g7.r1.l2 (TURN_LEDGER_FILENAME) in the same request and plausibly fixed r1.rule too.

Contrast in method quality: the single complete multi-turn read the agent performed (an `awk` line-range pull of the #code-review channel covering g7.r2.h1/rev1) produced a fully correct, unwavering r2.rule/scope, while every keyword-snippet search of the same kind of design-discussion channel left gaps at exactly the resolving sentence -- strong evidence that reading full exchanges rather than 1-2 line search snippets is what separates the facts this run got right from the ones it lost.
